scopeNotes: Native Land Digital lists Akaitcho as a territory linked to contemporary Dene organizations. The imported polygon surrounds Great Slave Lake and reaches northward; its exact historical extent remains unverified.
The map’s 1492 to 1500 interval does not date the modern regional organization or the lifetime of Chief Akaitcho. Community-specific evidence is identified in every example.
The 2000 agreement’s printed pages 2 and 3 were inspected as images. The territory is defined as asserted traditional and current land use, not a fifteenth-century state boundary.

The three PWNHC object displays are parts of one exhibition. Their combined paraphrase and notes remain below 200 words. Object labels were read from the public HTML annotations. No excavation provenance is invented.
The caribou coat is dated only to the 1970s; the decade marker is approximate. The net has no manufacture date.

The biography’s dated events are used, but its claim of Yellowknives disappearance is not adopted against contemporary community evidence. No exact peace-treaty year is selected from conflicting traditions.
The 2004 submission expresses the First Nations’ treaty understanding. The card does not purport to resolve contemporary legal title.
The 2022 wayfinding study explicitly distinguishes Yellowknives Dene and Gwich’in methods. Only the named Yellowknives account is used here.
No unverified successor links or precise ancient founding date are supplied. Independent historical and geographical review remains pending.
